defects: Narrow and shorten the pool and mark an accessible perimeter from the entrance to the rear hall. Its surround leaves only about 0.0165 units beside each dormitory plinth, and its rear overlaps the hall plinth.

models.observations: The long reptile muzzle, spread turquoise frills, gold eyes and crowned sun clearly read as a carved creature. Paired votives and a stair serve the low, grounded plinth throughout Dawn, Bronze and Iron. Serialized validation passes all three LODs.
The iron-age stone terraces and steep dark cap give a clear, low stepped temple. Only tips of the two front votives emerge from the higher battered tier. Serialized validation passes all three LODs.
defects: Seat the two votives on exposed lower-terrace stone. At z=-0.367 their bases lie inside the next battered course. Moving them toward z=-0.53 should expose the cups and preserve the stair.

models.observations: Medieval and Renaissance sun marks now sit into both stone pylons. Their gold faces remain visible below the narrow turquoise collars, framing the central entry. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The pair of seals is seated on the lower faces of the pale cathedral pylons. The glass spires and halo continue to read clearly in both future ages. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

In both brick and Modern facade variants, the tower badges meet their battered walls beneath the teal collars. The twin offering lights still flank the approach. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

The reduced lily pool has paved walks to either side and a clear rear landing. The Classical, Renaissance and Medieval images all retain the courtyard and distinct roof lantern. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The short, narrow pool and paved walk now connect the gateway and the rear hall. The small lilies remain visible amid the blue glass roofs. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The paved route runs past the pool to the brick or concrete sanctuary door, and the two long dormitories remain legible around the open court. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

The sun idol's face now shows beneath the thatch at both preview sizes in Bronze and Iron. The platform has a clear staircase and a pair of tiny offerings. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

Gold and turquoise on the lowered shrine idol now read against the open bay in all three ages. The four posts and tile crown frame the altar without occluding it. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

Both futuristic rows retain the glazed canopy while revealing the idol's gold disc against its turquoise body. The center bay and stairs serve the same axis. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

The lowered idol now reads beneath the steel canopy in Industrial and Modern. The dark roof and illuminated sun face provide a clear hierarchy at 64 px. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The two complete votive cups stand on the exposed turquoise-edged terrace. The central stair remains open beneath the Iron-age timber cap. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

Both gold cups flank the stair on the lower terrace. Their bases remain visible against Classical, Medieval and Renaissance masonry beneath the terracotta dome. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
On the pale lower terrace both lamps read in front of the battered course. The twin sky-blue supports and halo remain distinct at 64 px. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The two votives now sit visibly outside the upper course on both the brick and concrete temples. The entry and broad axial stair remain legible. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

Two long cloister roofs flank a bright inner court and lead toward a distinct central bell roof. The court stays visible between the outer porch posts on the middle mesh. All three palettes retain the path and tower. The serialized meshes have 1365, 777, 217 triangles in LOD0/1/2. Against 91863de, the revised LOD1 changes 1.51% of front-view pixels and 1.90% of reverse-view pixels at 64 px (channel difference above 10).

Two domed cells and a high gold arch frame a turquoise courtyard basin. At 64 px the twin rooms, arch opening and near-edge pool read as separate forms. The earlier linear cloister and pointed bell roof have been replaced. The serialized meshes have 1028, 582, 192 triangles in LOD0/1/2.

A square bell tower stands alongside a low barrel-roof hall, with a covered walk and a visible pool below. The tower remains separated from the hall even in the reverse far view. The asymmetrical layout breaks the older paired cloister wings. The serialized meshes have 756, 449, 200 triangles in LOD0/1/2.

rounds.critic: Independent visual critic, frozen middle-LOD fidelity review
rounds.inspection: Inspected current age previews and all three serialized LODs at phone scale. Examined the middle mesh from the front, side and rear at larger scale and compared individual entrances and surfaces against LOD0. Rechecked the serialized catalog metadata, triangle ratios, exposed surfaces and shell orientation. Existing design scores were retained for unchanged designs that remained legible.

models.observations: Three roofed ranges remain around the small blue courtyard pool. Their back walls and roof edges stay connected, and the sheltered doors remain visible from the front.
